summary: Richard J. Davidson studied at Midwood High School, New York University (~1968–1972), and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 and 1996, serving there as a psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988 under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and also studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Richard K. Payne studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1996–2018) and was a Core Doctoral Faculty member at the Graduate Theological Union (~1996).

Richard Keith Sprigg worked in linguistics and Tibetology. After studying at Oakham School (~1935–1940), he held posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London from circa 1948 to 1982.

Richard Kieckhefer, a scholar of religious studies and history, studied at Saint Louis University, the University of Texas at Austin, and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. He joined Northwestern University in 1975 and served as president of Societas Magica and the ASCH.

Richard King works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster University under Daniel Mariau, and held posts at the University of Stirling (~1993–2003), Vanderbilt University (~2003–2008), and the University of Glasgow (~2008–2012).

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1994–2001) before serving as Professor of Religious Studies at Duke University (~2001).

Richard Morris worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Battersea Training College. He held positions at King's College School, Dedham Grammar School, the Philological Society (~1874–1875), and the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888).

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under traditional teacher Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

Richard P. Hayes studied at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, Shoryu Katsura, and T. Venkatacharya. He held posts at the University of Toronto, Leiden University, McGill University (attested 1997–2009), and the University of New Mexico (attested 2011–2016).

Richard Payne is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996, 2007) and held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2021).
Richard Peter Hottelet was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1971).

Richard Phené Spiers was an architectural historian and archaeologist. He studied at King's College London from circa 1855 to 1858 and at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts from circa 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He held chairs and posts at Kiel University (1875), the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1885–1902), the Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1908), and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Richard Polenberg, an American history scholar, earned degrees from Brooklyn College (~1955–1959) and Columbia University (~1959–1964). He was Professor of American History at Cornell University (1966–2011) and a Fulbright Visiting Professor at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1978–1979).

Richard S. Cohen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Walter M. Spink and Luis Oscar Gómez. He serves as Associate Professor of South Asian Religious Literatures at the University of California, San Diego.

Richard Schechner studied at Cornell University (~1952–1956), the University of Iowa (~1956–1958), and Tulane University (~1959–1962). Around 1967, he became a University Professor at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts.

Indologist Richard Schmidt studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg under Ernst Mehliß, Richard Pischel, and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Privatdozent at Halle-Wittenberg (~1898–1909), librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1904–1910), and ordinary professor at Münster (1910).
Richard Shilleto, who worked in linguistics, completed his education at Repton School, Shrewsbury School (~1823–1828), and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1828–1832).

Richard Sorabji studied at Dragon School, Charterhouse School, and Pembroke College, Oxford (~1953–1957). In philosophy and Indology, he held posts at Cornell (~1962–1970), King's College London as Professor (~1970–2000), and Gresham College (~2000–2006).
